summary: Bradford's public content frames Toronto taxes and fiscal policy around a "paying more, getting less" theme, citing cumulative property tax increases of roughly 25% over three years under Mayor Chow (DTc0JOhlNtb, DE2RXwfRFVN, DExr-I1yGsL). Bradford opposes tax increases above inflation (DFdqfBhSsqJ), opposes the Vacant Home Tax and the luxury/land transfer tax hike (DW2FRA0ANLp, DSabj0Mjkvw, C56wHybPF4Q), and characterizes reserve draws of $512M as unsustainable, predicting a 10.5% tax increase to follow (DUl96QKkebM, DT3EAOSkTOp). Bradford supports property tax cuts for industrial properties and small businesses (DIcIi5byoAH, DF6VebxtJGc, C3GD7yhgljQ), open tendering projected to save $200M annually (CsUNNf3AEZE), a fair intergovernmental fiscal deal (Cw2crzygFOv, CxLVkkfg2GY), and value-for-money reviews. Earlier posts (2021) reflect a role as Budget Committee Vice-Chair announcing efficiency-focused budgets (CLdC-GVhur1, CKB18vvjD_9).

key_positions.stance: Opposes property tax increases above the rate of inflation, citing cumulative ~25% rise over three years.
Opposes the Vacant Home Tax as bureaucratic, ineffective, and a 'tax grab'; proposed suspending/shelving it.
Opposes drawing ~$512M from reserve funds to balance the budget, characterizing it as unsustainable and likely to force a 10%+ tax hike the following year.
Supports property tax cuts for industrial properties and small businesses (proposed a 25% cut).
Supports using tax stabilization reserves for genuine emergencies such as a US trade war/tariffs, while opposing routine reserve draws.
Opposes the luxury home/land transfer tax hike on homes over $3M.
Supports open tendering for city contracts, projected to save at least $200M annually.
Supports a new intergovernmental fiscal deal so Toronto is not solely reliant on property taxes and user fees.
Supports value-for-money scrutiny and finding efficiencies before raising taxes.
Supports property tax relief/subclasses for specific sectors (live music venues, small businesses).
